Paul Sand

Libertarian candidate for Governor, Idaho · Challenger

Retired computer software engineer; former White Bird city councilmember

Paul Sand is the Libertarian nominee for Governor of Idaho and served 10 years on the White Bird City Council. He filed on February 23, 2026, and won the May 19 Libertarian primary over Melissa-Sue Robinson, 523 votes (57.16%) to 392. This is his second run for governor; he was also the Libertarian nominee in 2022 and received 1.1% of the general election vote.

Where Sand stands

Budget and governing approach
Proposes letting counties with similar social and economic profiles form self-governing federations, each with its own rules, regulations, taxes and budgets, so that each one decides which social programs to fund.
Taxes
Says state departments, including the executive branch, can be cut by 99% and that Idaho's state income tax and sales tax can be eliminated.
Role of the Legislature
Proposes that the Legislature meet one week per year, approve only the highway department/state patrol and Secretary of State budgets, and be paid the federal minimum wage for that week.
Rural-urban divide
Says his only priority is to permanently end the division between conservative rural counties and liberal urban counties. Argues that state government has never worked for rural Idahoans.
Growth and economic development
Opposes state policies meant to bring more businesses and people into Idaho, and says rural residents do not want data centers or low-income housing developments. Suggests inviting eastern Washington and Oregon counties to join Idaho.
Public lands
Opposes efforts to privatize public lands, saying "Idaho is not for sale."

Background

  • White Bird City Council member, 2007–2017
  • Libertarian nominee for Idaho governor, 2022 (1.1% of the general election vote)
  • Won the 2026 Libertarian primary for governor with 57.16% of the vote
  • Computer software engineer, computer business entrepreneur and home builder; owner of Sandcastle Antiques
  • Has lived in White Bird, Idaho, for about 30 years; hometown Minneapolis, Minnesota
